lectures.title: Income from House Property — Basis of Charge, Deemed Owners & Annual Value

cards.title: Sections covered (Income-tax Act 2025)
cards.html:
House Property — Sections 20 to 25
  • 20income from house property
  • 21determination of annual value
  • 22deductions
  • 23arrears & unrealised rent
  • 24property owned by co-owners
  • 25interpretation — deemed owner
SecTopic
20Income from house property (charge)
21Determination of annual value
22Deductions from income from house property
23Arrears of rent and unrealised rent received subsequently
24Property owned by co-owners
25Interpretation — deemed owner

Rent from a house is taxed under the 3rd head, Income from House Property (IHP), in the hands of the owner (real or deemed) — not the tenant. If Mr Ram owns a house and lets it to Mr Mohan, Ram pays tax under IHP; if Mohan sublets it, Mohan's income is Other Sources, not IHP.

cards.title: Basis of charge — Section 20
cards.html:
Section 20 — taxable under 'Income from House Property' when
  • Building or land appurtenant
  • Assessee is the owner
  • Not used for his own business / profession

The annual value of any property consisting of buildings or lands appurtenant thereto, of which the assessee is the owner, is chargeable under the head “Income from house property”.

Exception: the portion of a property used by the owner for his own business or profession (whose profits are taxable) is not taxed as house property.

Three conditions: (1) building or land appurtenant to it, (2) assessee is the owner, (3) not used for own business/profession.

cards.title: Ownership — real owner vs deemed owner (Sec 25)
cards.html:
Ownership of the property
  • Real ownerproperty stands in his name
  • Deemed ownerSec 25
    • ① Transfer to a spouse
    • ② Transfer to a minor child
    • ③ Holder of an impartible estate
    • ④ Member of a co-operative society
    • ⑤ Person in possession of a property
    • ⑥ Person having right in a property for not less than 12 years

Real owner — the person in whose name the property legally stands. Deemed owners:

  1. Transfer to spouse without adequate consideration (not under an agreement to live apart) → transferor is deemed owner. E.g. Mr X transfers house to wife without consideration, let at ₹5L p.a. → husband taxable. But transfer to a divorced wife (or under agreement to live apart) → the wife is taxable.
  2. Transfer to a minor child without adequate consideration → transferor is deemed owner (e.g. minor child gets rent ₹9L → father taxable). Exception: transfer to a minor married daughter → the daughter is taxable.
  3. Holder of an impartible estate — deemed owner of all properties in the estate.
  4. Member of a co-operative society / company / AOP to whom a flat is allotted → deemed owner.
  5. Person in possession of a property under part-performance of a contract (possession taken, price paid, registration pending) → deemed owner.
  6. Person having a right in a property for not less than 12 years (lease of 12+ years) → deemed owner.

cards.title: Composite rent
cards.html:
Composite rentrent for the house + services / other assets
  • House + serviceslift, water, electricity, watch & ward, AC → split: house → IHP · services → Other Sources
  • House + machinery / furniture
    • Letting separablehouse → IHP · rest → PGBP / Other Sources
    • Inseparablewhole → PGBP / Other Sources

Rent charged for the house plus facilities/services or other assets:

  • House + services (lift, water, electricity, watch & ward, AC): split — house portion → IHP; services portion → Other Sources.
  • House + machinery/plant/furniture: if letting is separable, house portion → IHP and the rest → PGBP or Other Sources; if inseparable, the whole → PGBP or Other Sources.

cards.title: Annual value (Sec 21) — the four values
cards.html:
Annual ValueSec 21
  • MVmunicipal value
  • FRfair rent
  • SRstandard rent
  • ARactual rent

Computation of income from house property

Higher of MV & FR
→
Lower of that & SR = Expected rent (ER)
→
Higher of ER & AR = GAV
→
− Municipal tax = NAV
→
− 30% std. deduction − interest (Sec 22)
→
= Income from house property
  • Municipal Value (MV) — value fixed by the municipality (e.g. MCD) for levying municipal tax.
  • Fair Rent (FR) — rent a similar property in the same locality would fetch.
  • Standard Rent (SR) — maximum rent fixed under the Rent Control Act (court order); the owner cannot legally charge more.
  • Actual Rent (AR) — rent received/receivable for the let-out period.

cards.title: Format — Computation of Income from House Property

items.f: GAV − Municipal tax paid by owner during the year

cards.q: Explain the deemed owners of a house property under Section 25.
cards.a:
1. Individual transferring house to spouse (other than under agreement to live apart) or to a minor child (other than a married daughter) without adequate consideration.
  2. Holder of an impartible estate.
  3. Member of a co-operative society/company/AOP to whom a building is allotted.
  4. Person in possession under part-performance of a contract.
  5. Person acquiring rights (lease) in a building for 12 years or more.

cards.q: Mr X transfers his property to his divorced wife without adequate consideration; she receives rent of ₹2,00,000. Who is taxable? What if he transfers it to his (non-divorced) wife and it is let at ₹5,00,000 p.a.?
cards.a: Divorced wife — she is the owner → wife is taxable. Transfer to existing wife without adequate consideration → husband is deemed owner → husband is taxable.

cards.q: Mr X transfers his house to his minor child without adequate consideration (rent ₹9,00,000). Who is taxable? What if it is transferred to his minor married daughter (rent ₹2,00,000 p.m.)?
cards.a: Minor child → father (deemed owner). Minor married daughter → exception → daughter is taxable.

cards.q: What is composite rent and how is it taxed?
cards.a: Rent covering the house plus services or other assets. Services: house portion → IHP, service portion → Other Sources. Machinery/furniture: separable letting → split (IHP + PGBP/Other Sources); inseparable → entire amount under PGBP/Other Sources.

cards.title: Gross Annual Value (GAV)
cards.html:
FR₁ = higher of MV and FR
ER = lower of FR₁ and SR (no SR → ER = FR₁)
GAV = higher of ER and AR

cards.title: Municipal tax (MT)
cards.html:
Municipal Tax (MT)
  • MT paid by ownerallowed
    • (i) On paid basis
    • (ii) Self-occupied → MT not allowed
    • (iii) Any amount paid by owner → allowed
  • MT paid by tenantnot allowed

Municipal tax pays for roads, parks, sewage and garbage collection. Deduction from GAV:

  • Paid by owner → allowed, on paid basis — only if actually paid during the tax year (1-4-2026 to 31-3-2027), whether it relates to the current, previous or a future year.
  • Paid by tenant → not allowed.
  • Due but not paid → not allowed.
  • Self-occupied property → not allowed (NAV is nil).
  • Shared payment → only the owner's part. E.g. MT ₹4,000, half paid by tenant → deduct ₹2,000: NAV = 3,00,000 − 2,000 = 2,98,000.

cards.q: When is municipal tax deductible from GAV?
cards.a: Only when it is borne and actually paid by the owner during the tax year (any year's tax). Not allowed if paid by tenant, if due but unpaid, or for a self-occupied house.

lectures.title: Section 22 — Different Situations (Self-occupied, Let-out, Vacancy, Part SO, DLO)

cards.title: Six situations
cards.html:
Sec 22 — Different Situations
  • 1. Self-occupiedNAV = 0 · MT paid ✗
  • 2. Let out full yearnormal manner
  • 3. Let out part of year, vacant partER vs AR (vacancy rule)
  • 4. Let out part, self-occupied part of yearnormal manner (e.g. 4 LO, 8 SO)
  • 5. Self-occupied & let out on the basis of area% basis (e.g. 70% | 30%)
  • 6. More than two houses self-occupiedtwo SO · rest deemed to be let out (DLO)
  1. Self-occupied full year → NAV = 0; MT not allowed.
  2. Let out full year → normal computation.
  3. Let out part of year, vacant part → vacancy rule.
  4. Let out part, self-occupied part of year → treated as let-out for the year (normal manner).
  5. Part self-occupied, part let out by area → split everything in the area ratio (e.g. 60% SO / 40% LO).
  6. More than two houses self-occupied → any two treated as self-occupied; the rest are Deemed to be Let Out (DLO) — GAV = ER, AR = 0.

cards.title: Vacancy rule (let out part of year, vacant part)
cards.html:
Let out part of year, vacant part of year
  • AR ≥ ERGAV = AR
  • AR < ER because of vacancyGAV = AR
  • AR < ER for other reasons (low rent)GAV = ER
  • AR = rent for the let-out months only.
  • If AR ≥ ER → GAV = AR.
  • If AR < ER because of vacancy (i.e. the full-year rent would have been ≥ ER) → GAV = AR.
  • If AR < ER for other reasons (rent itself is low) → GAV = ER.

lectures.title: Calculation of Interest (Pre-construction Period) & Comprehensive Problems

cards.title: Interest u/s 22(1)(b) = current-year interest + pre-construction interest
cards.html:
Calculation of Interest22(1)(b) = current year + PCP
  • Normal interestcurrent year, simple manner
  • Pre-construction period interest (PCP)
    • Step 1calculate PCP time
    • Step 2calculate interest
    • Step 3divide in 5 equal amounts

PCP = the period whose interest benefit was not taken; it is counted up to 31 March just before the tax year of construction.

Example: loan 1-10-2022, construction completed 31-5-2026

26-27current year + PCP
→
27-28PCP
→
28-29PCP
→
29-30PCP
→
30-31PCP
  • Current-year interest — simple interest for the tax year (months the loan was outstanding).
  • Pre-construction period (PCP) — from the date of borrowing to 31 March immediately before the tax year in which construction is completed.
  • Steps: (1) count PCP months; (2) compute PCP interest; (3) deduct it in 5 equal instalments from the year of completion.
Loan 1-10-2024, completed 10-8-2026 → PCP = 6 + 12 = 18 months
Loan 31-3-2024, completed 2-2-2027→ PCP ≈ 24 months
Loan 1-6-2022, completed 5-5-2026→ PCP = 10 + 12 + 12 + 12 = 46 months

items.n: PCP ends 31 March before the year of completion

lectures.title: Arrears of Rent & Unrealised Rent (Section 23, Rule 21)

cards.title: Section 23 — arrears & unrealised rent received later
cards.html:
Section 23 — Arrears & Unrealised Rent received later
  • Taxabilityin the year received / realised — even if no longer the owner
    • Arrears of rent received from a tenant
    • Unrealised rent recovered later
  • Standard deduction30% of the amount · no other deduction
  • Arrears of rent or unrealised rent recovered later are taxable under IHP in the year of receipt — even if the assessee is no longer the owner.
  • Deduction: 30% standard deduction only; no other deduction.

cards.title: Unrealised rent — Rule 21
cards.html:
Unrealised Rent
  • When not recoveredless from GAV (but Rule 21)
  • When recoveredadd after all calculations · less std. ded. 30%

Rule 21: (a) tenancy bona fide (b) defaulting tenant vacated / steps taken (c) tenant not in another property of the assessee (d) legal proceedings taken, or AO satisfied they would be useless.

Rent payable but not paid and proved lost and irrecoverable, where:

  1. the tenancy is bona fide;
  2. the defaulting tenant has vacated, or steps taken to compel him to vacate;
  3. the defaulting tenant is not in occupation of any other property of the assessee;
  4. the assessee has taken all reasonable steps to institute legal proceedings (or satisfies the AO they would be useless).
  • Not recovered → deduct from actual rent while computing GAV.
  • Recovered later → add in the year of receipt, less 30%.

cards.q: State the conditions of Rule 21 for unrealised rent.
cards.a:
1. Tenancy is bona fide.
  2. Defaulting tenant has vacated or steps taken to make him vacate.
  3. Defaulting tenant not in occupation of any other property of the assessee.
  4. All reasonable steps taken to institute legal proceedings, or the AO is satisfied they would be useless.
